name: BACH_0340
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (100%)** · Confident · Read in turn
Conformal set holds Benign only; second model agrees [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 100%, Invasive 0% | Clear separation |
| Conformal set | {Benign} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 1.00 / 70th percentile | Typical input |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Both models agree |
| Similar cases | 4 of 5 Benign [F5] | Mostly agree |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (region 9) · ↑ invasive · Below-typical score lowers invasive association [F2] · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (regions 3, 6, 7) · ↓ invasive · Above-typical score points away from invasive [F3] · Weak
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 1, 9, 10) · ↓ invasive · High score; associated with lower invasive likelihood · Validated
- **Tumor cell fraction and nuclear size variation** (regions 0, 3, 10) · context · Both at or above 93rd percentile of reference; conflict with benign call [F7] · Measured
- **Mean nuclear area** (regions 0, 3, 10) · context · 0th percentile of reference images; small nuclei · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) includes 0, so unproven; no Unreliable concept drives this case.

## Could be wrong if
- High tumor-cell fraction and size variation signal atypia the benign call misses.
- Cells were measured in only 3 of 12 regions; similar case BACH_0138 is Invasive.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 0, 3, 10**: Confirm whether neoplastic-labeled nuclei are truly atypical.
2. **Region 9**: Look for stromal invasion; it is the concept's strongest region.
3. **Regions 3, 6, 7**: Check whether atypical cells stay confined within ducts.
